title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election for Tennessee's 7th Congressional District
description: Tennessee's 7th Congressional District will hold a general election on November 3, 2026, to elect a U.S. Representative following a mid-decade redistricting in May 2026 that redrew the state's congressional map. The incumbent, Republican Matt Van Epps, won office in a December 2025 special election following the resignation of former Rep. Mark Green, and now seeks a full term. The race carries heightened significance due to the new map, which was drawn by the Republican-controlled legislature and is being challenged in court as racially gerrymandered. The district, anchored in Middle Tennessee and including parts of Nashville and surrounding counties, is rated as Safe/Solid Republican by major nonpartisan forecasters, with voters favoring Donald Trump by over 20 points in 2024. The August 6, 2026, primaries will determine the Republican and Democratic nominees from fields of two and four candidates respectively, alongside two independents qualifying for the general election ballot.
polling_note: No public opinion polls for the 2026 general election in Tennessee's 7th Congressional District were found as of mid-2026. The district is rated Safe/Solid Republican by Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball.

candidates.name: Matt Van Epps
candidates.summary: Matt Van Epps is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 7th Congressional District, first elected in a December 2025 special election. A West Point graduate and former Army helicopter pilot who served in the 160th Special Operations Aviation Regiment, he previously served as Tennessee Commissioner of General Services and Deputy Chief Operating Officer in Governor Bill Lee's office. He is an America First conservative who supports extending the 2017 tax cuts, completing the border wall, and a peace-through-strength foreign policy.

candidates.name: Vincent Dixie
candidates.summary: Vincent Dixie is a Democratic member of the Tennessee House of Representatives, representing District 54 in Nashville since 2018, and a candidate for U.S. House in Tennessee's 7th Congressional District. He previously ran in the 2025 special election Democratic primary for the same seat. His campaign priorities include affordable housing, accessible child care and healthcare, a livable minimum wage, and gun violence prevention.

He is a Nashville businessman and entrepreneur who previously ran in the 2025 special election Democratic primary for the same seat. His campaign focuses on economic issues including healthcare costs, Medicaid expansion, and reducing prescription drug prices.

candidates.name: Joshua Warren Sales
candidates.summary: Joshua Warren Sales is a Democratic candidate for U.S. House in Tennessee's 7th Congressional District, running in the August 6, 2026, primary. He is an AP English teacher in Davidson County, a U.S. Army veteran with an honorable discharge, and a graduate of the University of Tennessee Knoxville (summa cum laude). His campaign emphasizes a working-class agenda, rejecting corporate PAC money, and proposes a detailed legislative plan of twelve self-financing bills covering healthcare, tax fairness, housing, and campaign finance reform.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polling exists for this race, so the forecast relies entirely on structural indicators. Those indicators strongly favor Republicans: the district backed Donald Trump by over 20 points in 2024; Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball all rate it Safe/Solid Republican; and incumbent Republican Matt Van Epps already holds the seat after winning the December 2025 special election. The mid-decade redistricting (May 2026) and ongoing court challenge to the map introduce some uncertainty, as does the fact that the August 6 primaries have not yet occurred (leaving the Democratic nominee and independent candidates still undetermined). However, no evidence in the provided data suggests a general-election environment that would overcome the district's strong Republican lean. On the current map and available information, Republicans hold an overwhelming advantage.
